differences.text: The `button` prop is flattened into attributes of the built-in trigger (`label`, `variant`, `size`, `icon`, `icon-only`, `tooltip`, `disabled`) and a `slot="trigger"` for a trigger of your own; `hasChevron` is `no-chevron`; `isMenuOpen`/`onOpenChange` are `open` and the cancelable `tct-open-change` (D-006, A§7.2). `children` is the default slot and data mode keeps the `items` property, as upstream.

Disabled rows stay in the roving order and can be focused with the arrow keys (APG menu pattern: 'disabled menu items are focusable'), so keyboard and screen-reader users discover them and hear them announced as unavailable. Upstream skips `aria-disabled` rows. Typeahead and the initial focus still skip disabled rows, as upstream.

Data-mode row fields: `onClick` receives the click event; `hasCloseOnSelect` is `closeOnSelect` (data-mode default true); `isDisabled` is `disabled`; `endContent` and `label` take text or a Lit template; `icon` is a registered icon name; `hasSpinner` is offered on submenu rows. Sections and dividers are unchanged.

The bottom-sheet presentation is data-mode only, as upstream ('compound children currently support popover only'); a compound menu with `presentation="bottom-sheet"` stays a popover and warns in development.

`click` on the host also bubbles from rows and includes the click that light-dismissed the menu: a native click cannot be swallowed. The layer stack still ignores that click for reopening (`toggleFromTrigger`), so the menu does not reopen.

The trigger carries `aria-controls` only for the built-in button (both ends share the shadow root); a slotted trigger relies on `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup`, because ID references never cross a shadow boundary (A§8.2). Focus rings on rows are drawn inset, so a scrolling menu never clips them.

Tecton menu: a 1px rule on the recessed popover fill, no drop shadow, an element (4px) corner; rows fill with the Tecton table-row hover role with a 2px corner, the highlight follows DOM focus (a mouse moving over a row focuses it), md rows are 6px of block padding; destructive rows use the error role (D-013, design/components/menu.md, theme components.ts `dropdown-menu`).

Checkbox and radio markers render the built-in `tct-checkbox-indicator` / `tct-radio-indicator` tags: a theme's `defineIndicators()` override is not honoured inside menus, because rendering a runtime-chosen tag needs `unsafeStatic`, which is only allowed in core/security. See the request on this entry.

requests.reason: PositionController writes `max-inline-size: 100%; max-block-size: 100%` on the layer. In a small `position-area` cell (a 0x0 pointer anchor at a viewport edge, a flyout near the screen edge) that clamps the layer to the cell, the browser never sees an overflow and never tries the flipped areas, so the menu spills off screen. Menus override it with `!important` rules in dropdown-menu/tct-menu-surface.styles.css (upstream puts the clamp on the inner surface: 'applying it to the anchor-positioned popover itself prevents Chromium from selecting flip-inline'). Proposed: an option `clamp: 'area' | 'none'` (default 'area'), or write the clamps on the element `surface()` returns only when its cell is large enough.
requests.diff: PositionOptions: + clamp?: 'area' | 'none'; #writeCss: skip the two max-* size writes when clamp === 'none'.

requests.reason: Menu markers cannot follow `defineIndicators()` theme overrides (DDMENU-08): a runtime tag needs a static template, and `unsafeStatic` is restricted to core/security. Proposed: a core helper `renderIndicator(name, theme, props)` returning a TemplateResult for the resolved tag, used by every owner of an indicator (menus, lists, checkbox inputs).

core.dropdown-menu.notes: Guides: [mwg:resilient-context-menus-and-nested-dropdowns] (anchor positioning + popover; the guide warns to add role=menu only with the full keyboard contract, which MenuKeyboardController provides) [mwg:accessibility] [mwg:spatial-navigation] [mwg:accessible-web-components] [mwg:animate-to-from-top-layer]. Size: the touch presentation's elements (bottom sheet, list, heading, Back button) are a lazy chunk (menu-sheet.define.ts) loaded the first time a menu resolves to the sheet, so a popover-only menu does not pay for them (the button and shared i18n code dominate the remaining ~75 kB gzip). Structure: the menu is one `popover="manual"` layer in the element's shadow root (the shared LayerController/PositionController path of tct-popover); the surface is `role=menu`; rows are light-DOM children slotted into it (compound) or shadow children (data), all discovered from the flat tree by `collectMenuItems`.
